title: Asymptotic breathers in the Manakov system
authors: Liming Ling, Boris A. Malomed, Yan-Hong Qin, Jin-Peng Yang, Hao-Jun Yin, Li-Chen Zhao
abstract: We construct vector (two-component) asymptotic Akhmediev breathers in the Manakov system, matching generalized modulational-instability (gMI) eigenmodes to decaying tails of the breather states. The branch-resolved matching provides analytical results linking the gMI-perturbation envelopes to the positions of the emerging breathers. Numerical simulations of the system with the focusing and defocusing nonlinearities corroborate the analytical predictions for each MI branch. We further develop the asymptotic theory for two-breather solutions generated by two independent gMI modes, linking their temporal separation to the input envelopes and interaction-induced shifts. Further numerical simulations reveal that breather patterns exhibit robustness in the presence of weak nonintegrable perturbations. These findings establish a framework relating experimentally controllable input modulations to the branch-selective formation and positioning of breathers in multicomponent nonlinear systems.
summary: This paper develops an advanced asymptotic theory to predict how localized initial modulations generate specific, stable structures called Akhmediev breathers in the Manakov system. By matching generalized modulational instability modes to the breather state, the authors provide analytical formulas for the breathers' emergence points. This framework offers a powerful tool for controlling nonlinear wave dynamics, relevant for applications in optics and quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a predictive framework linking a localized initial perturbation to the exact location and structure of emerging Akhmediev breathers (ABs) in nonlinear wave systems.
main_result: The authors established an analytical, branch-selective theory that predicts the emergence and positioning of vector ABs, which was corroborated by numerical simulations.
method: The core method involves developing a branch-resolved asymptotic theory by matching generalized modulational-instability (gMI) eigenmodes to the pre-formation expansion of the asymptotic vector AB state.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Manakov system, a two-component integrable nonlinear-wave model, which governs coupled field components. The analysis extends to nonintegrable systems by including weak perturbations.
key_observables: Breather center positions and trajectories, total density $|q^{[1]}|^2$, and the temporal separation between multiple emerging breathers.
important_parameters: The nonlinearity parameter $\sigma$ (focusing/defocusing), the input perturbation envelope $f(x)$, and the gMI growth rate $G$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a locally matched asymptotic construction, assuming the perturbation envelope $f(x)$ has bounded logarithmic derivatives and remains non-zero.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the asymptotic AB excitation in both defocusing and focusing regimes, comparing predicted trajectories with numerical results. Figure 2 shows the evolution of two-AB excitations, comparing unperturbed versus nonintegrable scenarios.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the single-breather formation theory via gMI matching, then extending this framework to derive analytical predictions for two-breather solutions, and finally demonstrating the robustness of these patterns under weak nonintegrable perturbations.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, analytically derived mechanism to control the formation and placement of localized energy structures (breathers) in complex nonlinear wave systems, which is highly relevant for understanding light propagation in optical fibers or in Bose-Einstein condensates.
